answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Written in a bullet-like short clauses, then a summary line register, it stays short. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts split across independent auditors. The ember holds work receipts rather than names, so the tundra of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Reaching the grove of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys.
